# SyWare's UX patterns

The principles every SyWare app follows, then the pattern pages in reading order, each in full in `patterns/`.

## Principles

- **People stay in control**: The app proposes, people decide. Nothing that matters happens unseen; what cannot be undone asks once, and what can be undone offers Undo.
- **Answer before they ask**: Every screen says what it is, what state it is in and what can be done next. Every action gets an answer: a change on the page, a toast, or an error that says how to put it right.
- **Same task, same way**: A list, a form, a confirmation look and work the same in every app, with the same words in the same places. What people learn in one app works in the next.
- **What needs you comes first**: Home pages, lists and counts open on what waits for the person: reviews to decide, orders to prepare. Everything else is one step away.
- **Fast for regulars, clear for newcomers**: Ctrl K, shortcuts and dense lists for the people who use an app all day; plain words, empty states that teach and good defaults for their first visit.
- **Where the work is**: At a desk or in a warehouse: the tasks done away from a desk are made for a thumb first, and every other one still works on a phone.

## Pages

- **[Navigation](patterns/navigation.md)** (`navigation`): The frame of an app, page titles and addresses, back links and roles. Every SyWare app has the same frame: the same places for the product, the search, the destinations and the person, on a computer and on a phone. Learn it in one app, and find your way in all of them.
- **[Page layout](patterns/page-layout.md)** (`page-layout`): The page header, the widths, sections and cards, home pages and work surfaces. Before anything else, a page answers three questions: what is this, what state is it in, and what can I do here. Its header answers them, in the same place on every page.
- **[Lists and tables](patterns/collections.md)** (`collections`): Tables, rows or cards; search, filters, sort and long lists. Most of the work in an app starts by finding something in a collection. A collection looks and behaves the same everywhere: the same toolbar, the same rows, the same way to open an item.
- **[Actions](patterns/actions.md)** (`actions`): One primary action, the shared verbs, where actions go, and when they are disabled. An action says what it does, sits where people expect it, and looks as important as it is. The same action has the same name and the same place in every app.
- **[Forms](patterns/forms.md)** (`forms`): The four ways a form saves, layout, checking answers and leaving a form. A form asks only what it needs, keeps what people typed, saves in a way they can tell, and shows what is wrong where it is wrong.
- **[Loading, empty and errors](patterns/states.md)** (`states`): What a page shows before, without and instead of its content. A page is never blank and never silent. While it loads, it shows its shape; when it has nothing, it says why and what comes next; when something fails, it says what and offers a way on.
- **[Feedback](patterns/feedback.md)** (`feedback`): The result on the page first, toasts, progress and live updates. Every action gets an answer people can see. Most often the page itself changes; when it cannot show the result, or the result happens elsewhere, a toast says so.
- **[Confirm and undo](patterns/confirmations.md)** (`confirmations`): Which actions ask first, which offer Undo, and how they say it. People must be able to act fast without fear. What can be taken back is done at once and offers Undo; what cannot asks once, and names what will be lost.
- **[Dialogs and panels](patterns/overlays.md)** (`overlays`): When to use a page, a dialog, a drawer, a popover or a split view. Each surface has its job. Chosen by that job, it tells people what will happen: a dialog comes back to where they were, a page has an address, a drawer keeps the list in view.
- **[Status](patterns/status.md)** (`status`): The names, colours and icons of states, the same in every view and every app. Orders, runs and reviews go through states. Each state has one name, one colour and one icon, defined once, and shown the same way wherever it appears.
- **[Search and shortcuts](patterns/search.md)** (`search`): The command palette on Ctrl K, and the keys every app shares. Ctrl K (⌘K on a Mac) opens the same command palette in every app: it finds anything by its name or number, and does anything the person may do, without leaving the keyboard.
- **[Phones and touch](patterns/phones.md)** (`phones`): Phone tasks, thumbs, layouts that fold, cameras. Some work happens away from a desk: picking in a warehouse, ordering on a building site, deciding between two meetings. Those tasks are made for a phone first, and every other one still works on it.
- **[Accounts and settings](patterns/accounts.md)** (`accounts`): Signing in, the session, My account apart from Settings, theme and language. Signing in, choosing a password, changing the theme or the language: people do these in every app, so they look and read the same in all of them.
- **[Checklist](patterns/checklist.md)** (`checklist`): What to check before a screen ships. Go through it for every new screen, and when reviewing one. Each group leads to the pattern behind it.
